result: In a large flow-cytometry cohort, ME/CFS patients under 50 had a higher CD4/CD8 ratio, more CD8+ effector-memory cells and fewer NK cells; across ages Th17 and MAIT cells secreted less IL-17/IFNg/granzyme A, Tregs were more frequent, and a random forest identified 93% of patients.
reason: Measures subset frequencies and cytokine secretion, not exhaustion transcriptional/chromatin programmes; closest is the MAIT/CD8-memory-subset flow finding

result: Self-rated SicknessQ scores in ME/CFS (n=38, mean 16.1) and chronic pain (n=190, 16.1) matched LPS-injected healthy subjects at peak inflammation (16.3) and exceeded primary care (10.7), general population (5.4) and healthy controls (3.6).
reason: Cross-sectional questionnaire of sickness behaviour; finding is about acute-infection severity and cytokines predicting post-infective fatigue, and no atlas finding covers SicknessQ

result: In a retrospective series of 123 ICC patients, 44.7% had at least one resting blood lactate >=2 mmol/L, and this group had more severe PEM (adjusted OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.10-5.55).
reason: Adds a resting-lactate subgroup linked to PEM severity; weak (no controls, retrospective, resting not per-watt measure)

result: Serum GDF15 was higher in severe ME/CFS (602 pg/ml, n=50) than healthy controls (491 pg/ml, n=150; P=0.01), only marginally raised in mild/moderate (560) and MS (546), correlated with fatigue (P=0.026), and was stable over about 7 months.
reason: GDF15 is covered by the newer muscle-exertion-gdf15 finding; this adds resting levels, a severity gradient and stability

result: Home EEG in 24 CFS vs 24 matched controls showed slower sleep onset, more awakenings and more slow-wave sleep, with reduced normalized HF-HRV especially in deeper sleep that tracked poorer self-reported sleep quality and wellbeing.
reason: Same objective sleep measures in the same direction as the meta-analysis (longer SOL, more WASO, more N3), plus per-stage autonomic data

result: Normalized high-frequency HRV was lower in 24 CFS than 24 controls, mainly during deep sleep, not during wake before sleep, and lower deep-sleep parasympathetic activity went with poorer sleep quality and wellbeing.
reason: Nocturnal, sleep-stage-specific HRV fits the dedicated nocturnal HRV finding better; reduction was absent at resting wake, so not a clean extension of the resting HRV claim

result: Circulating EV counts were higher in ME/CFS and correlated with CRP and antioxidant potential (AUC 0.80), and proteomics in two analyses found talin-1, filamin-A and 14-3-3 proteins as the most abundant ME/CFS-specific EV proteins compared with controls, idiopathic chronic fatigue and depression.
reason: Same measure (EV count, same direction) plus EV protein candidates; no multiple-testing or independent-replication detail, consistent with the finding's caveat

result: Whole-cell patch-clamp in IL-2-stimulated NK cells from 8 ME/CFS patients vs 8 matched controls confirmed impaired PregS-evoked TRPM3 currents, and 24 h of naltrexone restored TRPM3 activity without acting as a direct channel agonist.
reason: Same measure and direction, but from the same group with n=8, so not independent replication; the new content is in vitro naltrexone restoration

result: Whole-cell patch-clamp in IL-2-stimulated NK cells from 8 ME/CFS patients vs 8 matched controls confirmed impaired TRPM3 currents, which naltrexone restored in vitro.
reason: Functional NK-cell study with no genotyping; belongs with the immune TRPM3 functional finding, not the genetics one

result: Resting and task fMRI in 45 Fukuda ME/CFS vs 27 controls found reduced connectivity between medulla and cuneiform nucleus and from brainstem to hippocampus and intralaminar thalamus during task only, with weaker RAS connectivity related to worse symptom severity.
reason: Same brainstem connectivity measure (medulla-cuneiform) as Inderyas 2026 in a different cohort; same Griffith group, so not fully independent
